title: Montville's Diwali Drive Passes $7,000 for the Township Food Pantry
excerpt: Deepa Venkatraman's second annual 'Light Up Lives for Diwali' fundraiser has drawn in a whole New Jersey township — and the pantry is adding hours to meet rising demand.
body:
• A Diwali fundraiser started by Montville, New Jersey resident Deepa Venkatraman has raised more than $5,500 for the Montville Kiwanis Food Pantry, with a $1,500 matching gift taking the total past $7,000.
  • The second annual 'Light Up Lives for Diwali' drive runs through Sunday, November 8, and donations are being taken online through the pantry's own Zeffy page.
  • The drive began in a WhatsApp group for Montville's South Asian residents — about 18 percent of the township's population — and spread to neighbours of all backgrounds.
  • The pantry, an all-volunteer operation, says demand is rising and is adding Friday distribution hours, 12 p.m. to 2 p.m., starting this month.

A course project turned into one of the larger Diwali fundraisers in Morris County. Deepa Venkatraman, a Montville resident pursuing her second master's degree, in social work, at Rutgers University, spent a summer course examining food insecurity in her own county — and came away, she told TAPinto, struck by the contrast between everyday spending, like buying coffee several times a week, and neighbours struggling to put food on the table. The result is the second annual "Light Up Lives for Diwali" drive for the Montville Kiwanis Food Pantry.

Past $7,000, with days still to run

The drive has collected more than $5,500 in community donations so far, and Dr. Sunil Shah, a board member of the Montville Kiwanis Club, has offered a $1,500 matching contribution — taking the total past $7,000 as the campaign enters its final days, TAPinto reported. The fundraiser launched on September 16 and runs through Sunday, November 8, Diwali day. Donations are made through a zero-fee online platform hosted directly by the pantry, so the full amount reaches the organisation.

"Diwali is a time of giving. You don't necessarily have to be of a specific religion to be able to participate in that giving spirit."

— Deepa Venkatraman, organiser

From a WhatsApp group to a township

Venkatraman first tested the idea in a local WhatsApp group for South Asians living in Montville — a community that makes up roughly 18 percent of the township's population, according to census figures cited by TAPinto. The response carried the drive well beyond that network, with neighbours from various backgrounds joining in. "We are incredibly grateful for the remarkable outpouring of support for the second annual Diwali Fundraiser," said Danielle Mangione-Vasser, president of the Montville Kiwanis Club, adding that the support arrived at an especially important time as demand grows.

Why the pantry needs it now

The Montville Kiwanis Food Pantry, at 91 Passaic Valley Road, is an all-volunteer organisation run in connection with the Montville Kiwanis Club and serves as a monthly food resource for township households — including, the pantry says, many families turning to it for the first time. To meet the growing demand, it is expanding its distribution schedule starting in November, adding Friday hours from 12 p.m. to 2 p.m.

How to help

To support the drive, donate through the pantry's Light Up Lives for Diwali donation page — the campaign, organised by Deepa Venkatraman to stock the Montville Kiwanis Food Pantry through the festival season, runs until Sunday, November 8. It is a local version of a pattern repeating across the diaspora this Diwali, from food-bank packing events to temple drives: the festival of lights, marked by giving food as well as by lighting lamps.
